title: Information under special-bit conditioning
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $p$ be a deterministic protocol for disjointness on inputs of length $n$. Under the hard distribution conditioned on disjoint inputs, let $X_T$ be Alice’s bit at the special coordinate, let $M$ be the transcript of $p$, and condition on $(T,X_{<T},Y_{\geq T})$. The conditional mutual information under the further conditioning that Bob’s special-coordinate bit is false, multiplied by $2/3$, is at most the conditional mutual information under the disjointness-conditioned distribution.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a deterministic protocol on length-$n$ disjointness inputs
The base distribution is conditioned on disjoint inputs
The further conditioning is that Bob’s special-coordinate bit is false
replaced:
Fix a positive integer $n$ and a deterministic communication protocol $p$ for
disjointness inputs of length $n$. Consider the hard distribution over samples
conditioned on the generated input pair $(X, Y)$ being disjoint, and let $M$ be the
transcript that $p$ produces on that input, $X_T$ Alice's bit at the special coordinate
$T$, and $(T, X_{<T}, Y_{\ge T})$ Alice's corrected special-coordinate conditioning
variable. Writing $I_D(X_T : M \mid T, X_{<T}, Y_{\ge T})$ for the conditional mutual
information under this disjoint-conditioned distribution, and $I_{D_0}(X_T : M \mid T,
X_{<T}, Y_{\ge T})$ for the same conditional mutual information under the distribution
obtained by further conditioning on Bob's special bit $Y_T$ being false, one has
\[
\tfrac{2}{3}\, I_{D_0}(X_T : M \mid T, X_{<T}, Y_{\ge T}) \;\le\; I_D(X_T : M \mid T,
X_{<T}, Y_{\ge T}).
\]
